subject: Post-call recap: burn curve, pricing options & multi-year credit proposal
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire@nimble.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: burn curve, pricing options & next steps

Hi Claire — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can put a formal proposal together: 

Call highlights:
- Primary workload: conversational search + short generation for customer support (avg. seq len ~220 tokens).
- Current pilot traffic: ~600k tokens/week but expected growth to ~4–6M tokens/month over next 3–6 months based on your roadmap.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 450ms.

What we need to finalize pricing options:
1) Confirm expected token burn curve over the next 6 months (rough monthly figures are fine).
2) Target unit economics: what would you need $/1M tokens to look like to make a multi-month commit attractive? (ballpark is fine).
3) Any constraint on billing terms (Net-30, PO process, required PO number)?

Initial thoughts from our side (we'll refine after your numbers):
- Base spot-ish price: ~$20 / 1M tokens (example only) — committed bands improve that unit price markedly.
- Typical discount levers: committed monthly minimum, multi-year term, and startup/founder credit if eligible.

If you can reply with the burn estimate and whether you plan to seek startup program support (founder sponsorship / accelerator track), Ben and I will draft a few concrete pricing bands and a short commercial summary for procurement.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Claire Park <claire@nimble.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: burn curve, pricing options & next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks for the summary and the clarity. Quick answers below and attaching our simple burn model for reference (nimble_burn_model_Q2.csv).

Burn estimates (conservative -> aggressive):
- Month 1: 1.1M tokens
- Month 2: 2.8M tokens
- Month 3: 4.6M tokens
- Month 4: 5.2M tokens
- Month 5: 6.0M tokens
- Month 6: 6.8M tokens

Target unit economics: to justify a firm commit we need target in the ~$14–$17 / 1M tokens range. If you can get to that with a 12–24 month commit, we can propose it to our CFO.

Procurement: Net-30 is standard for us. We will need a PO and a signed SOW or order form. Procurement is looped (procurement@nimble.ai) and would like a clear "single line" cost for accounting.

Also: We're a YC-backed company (W23). Would Nimble qualify for Redwood's startup program or any founder credit? That would help tighten the economics while we ramp.

Appreciate it —
Claire Park
Head of Product, NimbleAI
claire@nimble.ai

Attachment: nimble_burn_model_Q2.csv

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire@nimble.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: burn curve, pricing options & next steps — proposed bands

Great context, Claire — thanks for the file. Based on your burn curve and startup status (W23), here are three tailored options we can put in a formal quote. I've attached a pricing worksheet (redwood_pricing_worksheet_v2.xlsx) that shows the math:

Option A — Ramp-friendly (6-month commit)
- Commitment: 5M tokens/month average over first 6 months
- Term: 6 months
- Effective unit price: $18.50 / 1M tokens (approx. 7.5% discount off base)
- Additional: +1 month free trial extension to help with ramp testing

Option B — Standard committed (12-month) — recommended
- Commitment: 5M tokens/month average (12 months)
- Term: 12 months
- Effective unit price: $15.80 / 1M tokens (approx. 21% off base)
- Additional: $5k founder credit applied in the first invoice (startup program credit)

Option C — Fast-growth (24-month)
- Commitment: 6M tokens/month average (24 months)
- Term: 24 months
- Effective unit price: $13.20 / 1M tokens (approx. 34% off base)
- Additional: priority capacity pool + quarterly cost review

Notes and constraints:
- Prices assume standard Redwood managed hosting and do not include optional dedicated capacity add-ons.
- We can do Net-30 invoicing and accept PO; legal will use our standard order form (I'll route procurement copy).
- Founder credit eligibility: since you're YC W23, you qualify for a one-time startup credit; I have to confirm the exact sponsor amount but I tentatively proposed $5k in Option B. We will earmark that in the quote.

Next steps: if you can indicate which option is most aligned (A/B/C) and confirm PO/billing owner, I'll: 
1) Draft a one-page commercial summary + order form for your procurement.
2) Put together a short SOW showing latency SLO and onboarding milestones.
3) Ben will run a short integration/latency test and confirm the p95 number in your environment.

Would you be available for a quick 20-minute sync tomorrow to walk this through with procurement?

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_pricing_worksheet_v2.xlsx

From: Claire Park <claire@nimble.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimble.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Post-call recap: burn curve, pricing options & next steps — proposed bands

Aisha — really helpful, thanks. A couple of quick clarifications before we lock an option: 
- Option B looks closest to what the finance team will consider. Can you confirm the monthly minimum floor? If we miss the committed minimum in a month, is it billed to the committed floor?
- Procurement asks whether Redwood can provide a Net-30 invoice and one consolidated line item for the monthly committed spend (we'll attach the PO to that line).
- On the startup credit: we will need a sponsor or program code to attach to the PO. Can you add that to the commercial summary?

Procurement is available for a 20-minute sync tomorrow at 10am PT if that works for your team.

Thanks —
Claire Park
Head of Product, NimbleAI

Attachment: (their burn model already attached)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire@nimble.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@nimble.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Re: Post-call recap: burn curve, pricing options & next steps — next steps and owner matrix

Thanks — 10am PT tomorrow works. Quick operational notes so procurement has everything upfront: 

What we'll send before the call (timeline: by EOD today):
- One-page commercial summary + single-line pricing (Option B highlighted). (owner: Aisha)
- Draft order form (Net-30, PO-friendly). (owner: Aisha / Legal)
- Pricing worksheet with month-by-month burn overlays (attachment we've already sent). (owner: Aisha)
- Integration/latency test plan and Ben's contact for execution. (owner: Ben)

Operational commitments from Redwood: 
- Monthly committed floor billing: yes — if monthly usage < committed minimum, customer is billed to the committed floor. We can include a true-up clause or allow a one-time overage credit if there is one off miss in month 1.
- Startup sponsor code: I'll confirm the program code with our partnerships team and include it in the quote (target: include it in the commercial summary so Procurement can reference it on the PO).
- Manager-level approval: Lauren can approve discounts up to 15%; anything higher will require revenue desk sign-off.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890 (RDW-2027-NIM-42) — I'll update with the selected option after our call.

See you tomorrow at 10am PT. If procurement wants the draft order form sooner, reply-all and I'll escalate.

Best —
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
